countess.line: To the countess who's pretending to care for him
countess.lineNext: Sayin', "Name me someone that's not a parasite
stanza: The peddler now speaks
To the countess who's pretending to care for him
Sayin', "Name me someone that's not a parasite
And I'll go out and say a prayer for him"
But like Louise always says
"You can't look at much, can you, man?"
As she, herself, prepares for him
And Madonna, she still has not showed
We see this empty cage now corrode
Where her cape of the stage once had flowed
The fiddler, he now steps to the road
He writes everything's been returned which was owed
On the back of the fish truck that loads
While my conscience explodes
The harmonicas play the skeleton keys and the rain
And these visions of Johanna are now all that remain

countess.linePrev: A shrieking, six-legged millionaire with a blight in his sockets
countess.line: Miss Montez, the Countess of Lansfeld
countess.lineNext: Appealed to the King of Bavaria
stanza: Miss Montez, the Countess of Lansfeld
Appealed to the King of Bavaria
Saying, "Pretty papa, if you are my friend
Mister Daddy Longlegs, they are at it again
Can I see you?"

countess.line: Poor Lola, a tarantula's mounting Countess Lansfeld's handsome brassiere
stanza: Poor Lola, a tarantula's mounting Countess Lansfeld's handsome brassiere
While they all cheer
And the old king fell from grace while Lola fled
To save face and her career
